name: Ridgeline 2P Tent
blurb: Two-person, three-season shelter with a quiet vestibule for wet gear.
description: A freestanding two-person tent with a full-coverage fly, dual doors, and a vestibule that actually fits muddy boots. DAC poles, taped seams, and a footprint-friendly rectangular floor.

name: Summit Down Jacket
blurb: 800-fill down, baffled through the core, with a helmet-friendly hood.
description: Built for alpine starts and windy ridgelines. 800-fill responsible down, a durable water-repellent shell, and a hood that still cinches over a beanie.

name: Granite Trail Boots
blurb: Leather and suede hikers with a sticky outsole for wet granite.
description: Full-grain leather uppers, a padded collar, and a lug pattern that bites into wet rock. Break them in on a weekend loop; they are ready for week-long miles.

name: Daybreak 28L Pack
blurb: A daypack with a stiff sheet, ice-axe loop, and a lid that does not flop.
description: Twenty-eight liters of honest volume, a foam back panel, and side pockets that hold a bottle you can actually grab while walking.

name: Ember Camp Stove
blurb: Folding canister stove with a wide pot support and a fine simmer.
description: Piezo ignition, a pressure regulator for cold mornings, and pot supports that do not fold under a full kettle.

name: Quartz 1L Bottle
blurb: Double-wall steel that keeps a spring cold through a long afternoon.
description: One liter, a leak-proof cap, and a powder-coated body that does not scream when it hits granite.

name: Nightfall Headlamp
blurb: Three hundred lumens, a red night mode, and a lockout switch.
description: USB-C rechargeable, IPX4, and a beam that throws far enough to pick a cairn without blinding your partner.

name: Merino Base Layer
blurb: 150-weight merino that layers under a shell without itching.
description: A set-in sleeve, a slightly longer back hem, and merino that still smells like nothing after a two-day push.
